tldr: Canada's Real-Time Rail went live, with Wealthsimple and KOHO among the early adopters, which resets expectations for instant payments. Elsewhere, tokenized and 24-hour trading, stablecoin rails and in-app bill splitting are gaining ground.

highlights.headline: Canada's Real-Time Rail launched, with Wealthsimple joining at go-live and KOHO bringing instant payments to its users; Interac also issued a statement on the launch.
highlights.why: Instant payments are now table stakes in Canada. Direct competitor Wealthsimple is already on the rail, so Simplii needs a clear RTR timeline and customer messaging.

highlights.headline: Venmo launched receipt scanning to split bills by item. Cash App also added a Pay by Bandana tag collaboration with Nahmias.
highlights.why: US peer-to-peer apps keep adding social and everyday-spending features. This raises expectations for how easy splitting and sending money should be, especially alongside Interac e-Transfer and RTR.

highlights.headline: PNC is launching stablecoin payments for corporate clients with Coinbase, which has also received a full US national trust charter. Stripe and miPlata launched a stablecoin Visa card.
highlights.why: Stablecoins are moving from crypto-native firms into regulated banks and card products. Simplii should watch whether Canadian banks and fintechs follow.

highlights.headline: NYSE plans to settle tokenized stocks on Avalanche. B3 is preparing tokenized share trading for 2027 and has presented a project for 24-hour blockchain trading.
highlights.why: Exchanges are signalling a shift toward tokenized, always-on trading. That could shape future expectations for Simplii's self-directed investing.
